title: A quantum switch of two lossy optical channels beats sending through both in sequence
problem: A quantum switch sends a system through two channels in an order controlled by a qubit, and with the control in superposition it can transmit information through channels that are useless one after the other. Earlier examples involved depolarizing and entanglement-breaking channels. Optical loss is the dominant noise in practice, and two pure-loss channels commute, which suggests the order should not matter. Does a switch of two identical pure-loss channels of transmissivity \(\lambda\) do better than passing the light through both, which is a single pure-loss channel of transmissivity \(\lambda^2\)?
result: It does, by a small margin, under a mean-photon-number constraint \(N\). The switch's output on a coherent state \(\ket\alpha\) is \(\ket{\lambda\alpha}\) together with a control qubit whose coherence is \(e^{-\kappa_\lambda|\alpha|^2}\), with \(\kappa_\lambda=(1-\lambda)(1-\sqrt\lambda)^2\). The control therefore carries information about \(|\alpha|\). This gives a strictly larger energy-constrained classical capacity for every \(N>0\) and \(0\le\lambda<1\), a larger quantum capacity for \(1/\sqrt2\le\lambda<1\), and a larger two-way assisted quantum capacity for \(0<\lambda<1\). For \(0.70578<\lambda\le1/\sqrt2\) the switch has positive quantum capacity while the sequential channel, with \(\lambda^2<1/2\), has none.
significance: This is the first example of causal activation for a continuous-variable channel, answering a question raised in earlier work on the switch. It shows that indefinite order helps even when the two channels commute, because the interference between the two orders depends on how many photons were lost. The exact output formula for coherent and thermal inputs makes such capacity comparisons computable.
limitations: The gains are small. Computed here, the classical gain at \(N=2\) is about \(0.05\) bits per use at \(\lambda=0.3\), \(0.0025\) at \(\lambda=0.7\) and \(0.0001\) at \(\lambda=0.9\). The activation window is only \(0.0013\) wide in \(\lambda\), with rates of order \(10^{-3}\) qubits per use. All capacities are lower bounds from particular inputs; optimal inputs and matching converses are open. The model is the abstract switch with independent environments and a control qubit delivered without noise, and it does not address how a switch of optical loss would be built. The author states that ChatGPT-6.1 Sol was used to assist with the derivation of the mathematical results and the bibliography research, and that all results were independently reviewed and checked.
summary_basis: Description based on the arXiv HTML of v1, read 2026-11-24: the main text and Appendices A, B, C (the strict-positivity argument in part) and E. Appendices D and F (quantum-capacity gain with thermal inputs and the two-way protocol) were not read in detail. Editorial checks: Eq. (5) was confirmed by applying the switch's Kraus operators directly in a Fock space truncated at 40 photons, at lambda = 0.6 and alpha = 0.9 + 0.4i, with deviation 4e-16. The classical gain Delta_N of Eq. (67) is positive at every tested point (N = 0.5, 2, 10 and lambda = 0.3, 0.7, 0.9). The threshold lambda* = 0.7057758 was reproduced as the root of lambda^2 = (1 − lambda)(1 + sqrt(lambda))^2 / 2. The coherent information of the restricted qubit channel, maximized over the diagonal input family, is 5.0e-4, 1.6e-3 and 2.8e-3 at lambda = 0.706, 0.7065 and 0.707, and negative at 0.7055.
methods_source_section: App. A (switch output for pure-loss channels, Eqs. (22)–(49)); App. B–C (Holevo quantity with a Gaussian coherent-state ensemble, Eqs. (50)–(79)); App. E (restricted qubit channel, degradability and activation, Eqs. (118)–(155))
methods_basis: Based on the linked paper version. Derivations marked as editorial, and suggested uses in other problems, are editorial guidance rather than results of the paper.
description: A pure-loss channel mixes the input mode with vacuum on a beam splitter of transmissivity \(\lambda\). Two in series give transmissivity \(\lambda^2\). In the switch, the control qubit starts in \(\ket+\), the mode passes through the two channels in the order \(\mathcal E\mathcal F\) on the \(\ket0\) branch and \(\mathcal F\mathcal E\) on the \(\ket1\) branch, and Bob receives both the mode and the control. Discarding the control returns the sequential channel, so the switch can never do worse; the question is whether keeping it helps.

The key computation shows that the switch output is a mixture over the number \(m\) of photons lost overall: the mode undergoes the \(\lambda^2\) loss channel's \(m\)-th Kraus operator, and the control is left in a state whose coherence is \(\gamma^m\), with \(\gamma=2\sqrt\lambda/(1+\lambda)\). The two orders differ in which channel lost which photons, so the more photons are lost, the less the orders interfere. For a coherent state the lost photon number is Poisson distributed, and averaging gives the control coherence \(e^{-\kappa_\lambda|\alpha|^2}\).

For classical communication the paper uses the Gaussian ensemble of coherent states that is optimal for a single loss channel. The Holevo quantity of the switch equals that of the sequential channel, \(g(N\lambda^2)\), plus a gain \(\Delta_N\) from the control, proved strictly positive. For quantum communication the thermal input gives a strictly larger coherent information whenever the sequential channel's capacity is reached by thermal inputs, which is for \(\lambda\ge1/\sqrt2\).

Below that, a restricted channel is used: inputs in the span of \(\ket0\) and \(\ket1\) only. This qubit channel has three Kraus operators, and it is degradable exactly when \(\lambda^2\ge\lambda_+=(1-\lambda)(1+\sqrt\lambda)^2/2\), that is \(\lambda\ge\lambda_*\approx0.705776\). In that range its coherent information is positive for diagonal inputs, so the switch's quantum capacity is positive, while \(\lambda^2<\tfrac12\) makes the sequential channel antidegradable with zero quantum capacity. With two-way classical communication, Bob measures the control in the \(\ket\pm\) basis, and distilling entanglement separately for each outcome beats the known two-way capacity of the sequential channel.

methods.technique: Exact switch output from products of loss Kraus operators
methods.explanation: Products of Kraus operators of two loss channels are proportional to single Kraus operators of the composed channel. Summing the two orders then separates into a loss channel on the mode times a control state that depends only on the total number of photons lost.
math: The loss channel has Kraus operators \(K^\lambda_m=\sqrt{(1-\lambda)^m/m!}\,\lambda^{\hat n/2}\hat a^m\). Using \(\hat a^i\lambda^{\hat n/2}=\lambda^{i/2}\lambda^{\hat n/2}\hat a^i\), \[K^\lambda_iK^\lambda_j=\sqrt{\binom{i+j}{i}\frac{\lambda^i}{(1+\lambda)^{i+j}}}\;K^{\lambda^2}_{i+j}.\] In the switch, the \(\ket0\!\bra1\) block pairs \(K_iK_j\) with \(K_jK_i\); summing over \(i+j=m\) gives the coefficient \(\sum_i\binom mi\lambda^{m/2}(1+\lambda)^{-m}=\gamma^m\) with \(\gamma=2\sqrt\lambda/(1+\lambda)\).

Hence \[\mathcal S_\lambda(\rho)=\sum_{m\ge0}K^{\lambda^2}_m\rho\,(K^{\lambda^2}_m)^\dagger\otimes\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&\gamma^m\\\gamma^m&1\end{pmatrix}.\] On \(\ket\alpha\), \(K^{\lambda^2}_m\ket\alpha\propto\ket{\lambda\alpha}\) with Poisson weight of mean \(\mu=(1-\lambda^2)|\alpha|^2\), so the coherence is \(\sum_me^{-\mu}\mu^m\gamma^m/m!=e^{-\mu(1-\gamma)}\). Editorial check: \((1-\lambda^2)(1-\gamma)=(1-\lambda)(1-\sqrt\lambda)^2=\kappa_\lambda\), and a direct Fock-space computation agrees to \(10^{-15}\).

For the thermal average \(\tau_N\) the output is block diagonal in photon number, with blocks \(\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}a_n&b_n\\b_n&a_n\end{pmatrix}\). Here \(a_n\) is thermal with mean \(N\lambda^2\) and \(b_n/a_n=c_n=\bigl[(1+N\lambda^2)/(1+(\lambda^2+\kappa_\lambda)N)\bigr]^{n+1}\). This gives the gain \[\Delta_N=\sum_na_n\,h_2\Bigl(\frac{1+c_n}2\Bigr)-\int\frac{e^{-|\alpha|^2/N}}{\pi N}\,h_2\Bigl(\frac{1+e^{-\kappa_\lambda|\alpha|^2}}2\Bigr)d^2\alpha,\] which the paper shows is the average excess relative entropy kept by the control, hence nonnegative by data processing and positive by an equality analysis.
methods.transfer: Rewriting products of Kraus operators of commuting channels as Kraus operators of the composite, with explicit weights, gives closed forms for switches and other coherent controls of Gaussian channels, such as amplifiers or thermal-loss channels.

methods.technique: Activation through a degradable qubit restriction
methods.explanation: Restricting inputs to vacuum and one photon gives a three-output qubit channel whose complement has the same form with one parameter swapped. Degradability follows exactly when the channel's parameter dominates, and then coherent information gives the capacity.
math: On \(\mathrm{span}\{\ket0,\ket1\}\) the switch has Kraus operators \(L_0=\ket{0,+}\!\bra0+\lambda\ket{1,+}\!\bra1\), \(L_1=\sqrt{\lambda_+}\ket{0,+}\!\bra1\) and \(L_2=\sqrt{\lambda_-}\ket{0,-}\!\bra1\), with \(\lambda_\pm=(1\pm\gamma)(1-\lambda^2)/2\). The output and its complement are \[\begin{pmatrix}\rho_{00}+\lambda_+\rho_{11}&\lambda\rho_{01}&0\\\lambda\rho_{01}^*&\lambda^2\rho_{11}&0\\0&0&\lambda_-\rho_{11}\end{pmatrix},\quad\begin{pmatrix}\rho_{00}+\lambda^2\rho_{11}&\sqrt{\lambda_+}\rho_{01}&0\\\sqrt{\lambda_+}\rho_{01}^*&\lambda_+\rho_{11}&0\\0&0&\lambda_-\rho_{11}\end{pmatrix},\] identical up to exchanging \(\lambda\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda_+}\).

A loss-like degrading map with transmissivity \(\eta=\lambda_+/\lambda^2\) on the middle level turns the first into the second, which needs \(\lambda^2\ge\lambda_+\). Comparing trace distances between the outputs for inputs \(\ket\pm\), \(\lambda\) for the channel and \(\sqrt{\lambda_+}\) for the complement, shows the condition is also necessary. Since \(\lambda_+=(1-\lambda)(1+\sqrt\lambda)^2/2\), it reads \(\lambda\ge\lambda_*\approx0.7057758\).

For degradable channels the quantum capacity is the maximal coherent information. For the input \((1-p)\ket0\!\bra0+p\ket1\!\bra1\) both outputs are diagonal and \[I_c=(1-\lambda_-p)\bigl[h_2(x)-h_2(y)\bigr],\qquad x=\frac{\lambda^2p}{1-\lambda_-p},\quad y=\frac{\lambda_+p}{1-\lambda_-p},\] positive exactly when \(x>y\), because \(x+y<1\). Editorial check: at \(\lambda=0.707\) the maximum over \(p\) is \(2.8\times10^{-3}\), at \(p\approx0.44\); the energy constraint requires \(p\le N\).
methods.transfer: Restricting a bosonic channel to a low-photon subspace and finding a degrading map there is a quick way to certify positive quantum capacity for coherently controlled or otherwise non-Gaussian optical channels.
